source_updates.title: CLEAN2FX: Label-Conditioned Modeling for Clean-to-Effect Guitar Audio Transformations
source_updates.revised_conclusion: U-Net gains are internal to a target-aware magnitude/Griffin-Lim/peak-normalized protocol and do not establish causal deployment, source-independent generalization, raw gain transfer, waveform fidelity or listener preference.

source_updates.title: A Production-Oriented Framework for Evaluation of SFX Generation
source_updates.revised_conclusion: The nine requirements are independent gates; current CLEAN2FX evaluation leaves identity, raw energy, targeted modification, robustness and efficiency unvalidated.

implementation_audits.name: fyp-clean2fx notebooks and inference path
findings: index-level random split shares the underlying source-note pool between train and test
the same 90/10 split drives ReduceLROnPlateau and final evaluation; no separate validation and untouched test
evaluation uses 20 first encountered examples per effect from one split without repeated seeds or uncertainty
clean input scaling depends on max(clean,target), which is unavailable at causal inference
deployment replaces oracle normalization with hard-coded effect corrections estimated on 50 training samples
FAD audio is independently Griffin-Lim reconstructed and peak-normalized per file
ConvVAE ratio-of-means is positive only because RAT dominates while 9 of 10 effects worsen
README source-of-truth CSV outputs are gitignored and absent; cache, dependency lock and root licence are missing

knowledge_cards.claim: Clean-plus-target normalization is an oracle path because target magnitude is unavailable at inference.
Effect-specific correction from 50 training examples is a deployment heuristic, not validated equivalence to benchmark normalization.
Index-random splits of synthetic sequences do not ensure source-note or pickup independence.
A split used to drive the scheduler is validation and must not also serve as untouched final test.
Twenty examples per effect from one selection without confidence intervals leave sampling uncertainty unknown.
Per-file peak normalization before FAD removes raw gain and energy-control information.
FAD on independently Griffin-Lim-reconstructed files conflates magnitude-model and phase-reconstruction error.
Original-waveform, unchanged-through-same-reconstruction and deterministic-processor baselines answer different questions.
Ratio-of-means can hide majority per-effect degradation and requires sign counts and dominant-class sensitivity.
ConvVAE worsens 9 of 10 effect MSEs; RAT alone creates its positive aggregate ratio-of-means.
Embedded notebook outputs without published CSVs, cache and pinned dependencies provide only partial reproducibility.
Identity rating that excludes loudness does not replace raw safety, musical quality or blind preference in mix.
